items.action: None, unless a global rule of yours at zero specificity (`*`, `:where(...)`) is meant to reach the elements inside library components and sets `box-sizing`, `font-family` on a form control, `margin` on a heading, or `outline`, `outline-offset`, `animation` or `border-radius` on a focused element: raise its specificity above zero, for example `:focus-visible` in place of `:where(:focus-visible)`.
items.appliesWhen: Ships in every library component's own stylesheet, and in `styles/component-base` for a component of yours that includes `component-base.rules`. A rule of yours above zero specificity wins as before. A zero-specificity rule ties with the base, and the component's stylesheet, inserted after your global styles, wins. The base sets nothing on `::before` and `::after`, so a rule of yours for them applies inside components, except on the `ds-button` spinner and the popover and tooltip arrows, which set `box-sizing: border-box` themselves.
items.pitfall: A custom ring written as `:where(:focus-visible) { outline: ... }` keeps showing on your own elements and loses only inside library components, which then show the library ring; check a focused `ds-button`, not your own markup.
items.verify: The built CSS of a library component holds `:where([_nghost-` and no `@layer`, and a custom focus ring of yours shows on a focused `ds-button`.

items.action: None, unless an empty state's title should run wider than 360px: set `--ds-empty-state-title-max-width: none` on that `ds-empty-state`.
items.appliesWhen: Every `ds-empty-state` with a `title`. The title was as wide as the component and is now capped at `--empty-body-maxw`, the body's width, and a word longer than a line breaks instead of overflowing.
items.pitfall: A title that fit on one line under the old width can now take two; check an empty state inside a wide card, not a narrow one.
items.verify: A `ds-empty-state` whose title is a 60-character word with no spaces wraps inside the component and adds no horizontal scrollbar.

items.action: Move each value into `[dsTooltipConfig]` on the same element and remove the old binding: `dsTooltipPlacement="right"` becomes `[dsTooltipConfig]="{ placement: 'right' }"`, `[dsTooltipDelay]` becomes `delay`, `[dsTooltipArrow]` becomes `arrow`, and a bare `dsTooltipPinOnClick` becomes `pinOnClick: true`; several go into one object. Where every tip of the app takes the same value, set it once in `provideDsConfig({ tooltip: { ... } })` instead.
items.appliesWhen: Elements carrying `dsTooltip` or `dsTooltipWhenClipped` that bind `dsTooltipPlacement`, `dsTooltipDelay`, `dsTooltipArrow` or `dsTooltipPinOnClick`. Not a `dsDefinitionTerm`: there `dsTooltipPlacement` stays the way to place the tip, and the term takes no `dsTooltipConfig`. `dsTooltip` and `dsTooltipWhenClipped` are not deprecated.
items.pitfall: A deprecated binding left beside `[dsTooltipConfig]` wins over the config field of the same name, so the tip keeps the old placement, delay, arrow or pin whatever the object says. A bare `dsTooltipArrow` or `dsTooltipPinOnClick` means `true`, so it moves as `arrow: true` or `pinOnClick: true`.
items.verify: No element with `dsTooltip` or `dsTooltipWhenClipped` binds `dsTooltipPlacement`, `dsTooltipDelay`, `dsTooltipArrow` or `dsTooltipPinOnClick` outside a `dsDefinitionTerm`, and each moved tip opens on the same side, after the same delay and with the same arrow as before.

items.action: None, unless your code reads `dsTooltipPlacement()`, `dsTooltipDelay()`, `dsTooltipArrow()` or `dsTooltipPinOnClick()` back from a `TooltipDirective`: handle `null` there, for example `tip.dsTooltipPlacement() ?? 'top'`.
items.appliesWhen: Code that holds a `TooltipDirective` instance, through `viewChild` or an injection, and reads `dsTooltipPlacement`, `dsTooltipDelay`, `dsTooltipArrow` or `dsTooltipPinOnClick`. Each was typed without `null` and read back its default when unbound; it is now `| null` and reads `null` when unbound. Binding the inputs in a template is not affected.
items.pitfall: A fallback such as `?? 'top'` gives the built-in default, not a value set through `dsTooltipConfig` or `DsConfig.tooltip`; read those from where your code set them.
items.verify: Every read of `dsTooltipPlacement`, `dsTooltipDelay`, `dsTooltipArrow` and `dsTooltipPinOnClick` in the app handles `null`, and the app type-checks under `strict`.

items.action: None, unless the app's tables must keep the 0.15.1 widths: set `provideDsConfig({ table: { layout: 'fixed' } })`, or `layout="fixed"` on one `ds-table`.
items.appliesWhen: Every `ds-table` without its own `layout`, in an app whose `DsConfig.table.layout` is unset, coming from 0.15.1 or 0.15.2; an app coming from 0.15.0 or earlier keeps the widths it had. Under `'auto'` each column follows its cell content as on 0.15.0: `kind` has no effect, and a numeric `width`, `width: 'content'`, `minWidth` and `truncate` size the column as on 0.15.0. A table with `virtualScroll` keeps `table-layout: fixed`. An app that already set `'auto'` sees no change.
items.pitfall: A `kind` or `minWidth` added for 0.15.1 does nothing under `'auto'`, so a table tuned for `'fixed'` changes width without a build error; check it with the app's real rows. `'auto'` is still deprecated, and a development build warns once per page while a binding or config key sets it.
items.verify: Without a `layout` anywhere, each `ds-table` shows the column widths it had on 0.15.0, and the console shows no `layout="auto"` deprecation warning.
evidence: command:node tools/table-clip-harness.mjs layout <0.15.0 docs url>/harness/table-clip <docs url>/harness/table-clip

informational.text: A `ds-table` under `layout="fixed"` or with `virtualScroll`, inside a container sized to its content (a `max-content` grid track, `width: max-content`, an inline-block, an absolutely positioned box without a width), is as wide as its columns at their declared widths and header labels, where it grew to 1 000 000px or to all the width there was. A table in a container with a width of its own is unchanged.
informational.verify: Put a ds-table with layout="fixed" in a div at width: max-content and confirm the table is as wide as its columns, not 1000000px.
evidence: command:node tools/table-clip-harness.mjs check <run of this checkout's /harness/table-clip> <run of the base's /harness/table-clip>

informational.text: The per-group select-all row of a `ds-multi-select` with `selectAll="group"` or `selectAll="both"` cuts its label to the panel width with an ellipsis, as the top select-all row does, so a long group name no longer scrolls the list sideways.
informational.verify: Open a narrow ds-multi-select with selectAll="both" and a long group name and confirm the group's select-all row ends in an ellipsis and the list has no horizontal scrollbar.

informational.text: `--ds-dropdown-panel-min-width` (default `0`) floors the whole `ds-select`, `ds-multi-select` and `ds-autocomplete` pane in both `width` modes, so a panel widened by it is placed by the width it is drawn at and stays on screen beside the right edge of the viewport; a wider trigger still sets the width. `--ds-dropdown-panel-max-width` applies only under `width="content"`; under the default `width="fill"` it no longer caps the panel.
informational.verify: Open a narrow ds-select and confirm its panel is as wide as its trigger, then set --ds-dropdown-panel-min-width: 220px on one beside the right edge of the viewport and confirm the 220px panel stays on screen.

informational.text: A `dsColumnSeries` in a `ds-chart` whose `cursor` is `'category'`, or resolves to it under `'auto'`, brightens the column at the category under the pointer, as a hovered column does under `cursor="none"`.
informational.verify: Hover a category of a ds-chart holding a dsColumnSeries and a dsLineSeries and confirm the column at that category brightens.

informational.text: The `ds-time-picker` hour and minute columns that hold more values than they show run on past either end: after the last value the first comes round again, the selected value is scrolled to the middle of its column, and the column shows no scrollbar. `loop="never"`, or `DsConfig.timePicker.loop: 'never'`, keeps them as lists.
informational.verify: Open a ds-time-picker, scroll the hour column past its last hour and confirm the first hour follows, then reopen it and confirm the selected hour sits in the middle of the column.

informational.text: `styles/ds` rings a focusable element the library does not render without giving it `--focus-ring-radius`: the ring follows the element's own `border-radius`, so an element of the app that declares none is no longer rounded while focused.
informational.verify: Tab to a square element of the app that sets no border-radius and confirm it keeps square corners while focused, then tab to a ds-button and confirm its ring is still rounded.

informational.text: The agent catalogue ships at `agent/INDEX.md` in the package, where it was `docs/agent/INDEX.md`; every leaf keeps its path under `agent/`. An agent rule or prompt that reads the catalogue from `node_modules` points at `agent/`.
informational.verify: Search the app's agent rules and prompts for `docs/agent/` and confirm none is left.

informational.text: A `dsTooltipWhenClipped` tip (`TooltipDirective`) also opens when its host's text is cut by lines, under `line-clamp` or a height with `overflow: hidden` or `clip`, as it did for text cut by width. A scroll box does not count.
informational.verify: Put dsTooltipWhenClipped on a block with -webkit-line-clamp: 2 holding four lines of text, hover it and confirm the tip opens; shorten the text to one line and confirm it does not.

informational: `ds-empty-state` takes `titleOverflow`: `'wrap'`, the default, keeps the title wrapping as before; `'clip'` keeps it on one line with an ellipsis and the full title in a tooltip.

informational.text: A printed `ds-pagination` shows only its range label: its page buttons, ellipsis and page-size select are left out of the printout, inside a `ds-table` and on their own.
informational.verify: Open the browser's print preview of a page holding a ds-pagination and confirm only its range label is printed.

informational: A printed `ds-table` keeps its column names on every page, keeps each row on one page and leaves its own controls out of the printout: the pager buttons and page-size select, the column filter, resize and expand buttons and the controls it adds to its toolbar. The pager's range label still prints. Nothing to change in consumer code; `printAllRows` opts a client-paged table into printing every row.

informational.text: `ds-table` takes `printHeading` and `printHeadingNote`: in print the table opens its header with a row holding the heading and the line under it, repeated with the header on every page. Both are hidden on screen; unset, the table prints as before.
informational.verify: Set printHeading and printHeadingNote on a ds-table of two printed pages, open the print preview and confirm both lines print above the column names on each page and do not show on screen.

informational: Every chart takes `highlightActive`, and `DsConfig.chart.highlightActive` sets it app-wide: `false` keeps the hovered or focused column, bar or heatmap cell at its own colour; unset falls back to the config, then `true`, which brightens it as before. An input on the element wins over the config.

informational.text: A column, bar or heatmap cell held by a click keeps its pin at its own colour once the pointer moves off it, and the mark under the pointer brightens instead; with nothing held, the hovered or focused mark brightens as before.
informational.verify: Click a bar of a ds-bar-chart to hold it, move the pointer to another bar and confirm the held bar is at its own colour and the hovered one brightens.

informational: Showing and hiding a tooltip, a chart tooltip, a modal, a confirm, a toast, a spinner, a skeleton or a loading overlay inserts and removes no stylesheet: the first instance keeps its sheet in the document for the life of the app.
